reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about precursor uniformity, reduction kinetics, nucleation, and resulting alloy homogeneity, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the detailed behavior of five-component noble metal systems under polyol conditions, so the lack of cited support leaves the key premises ungrounded.
premises: Molecular-scale precursor uniformity enables synchronized reduction and co-nucleation of multiple metal ions
Mechanically blended precursors cause spatial heterogeneity, asynchronous reduction, and localized nucleation
Synchronized co-nucleation leads to single-phase, homogeneous alloy nanoparticles
Asynchronous reduction and localized nucleation lead to phase separation and elemental clustering
